question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party, state institutions, and Central Military Commission as of mid-2026, with recent diplomatic engagements, New Year addresses, and elite appointments showing no signs of weakening authority. Analysts highlight the absence of a designated successor, extensive military purges that have removed potential rivals, and the lack of visible factional challenges or elite defections as key stabilizers ahead of the 21st Party Congress in 2027. This environment underpins trader consensus that removal before the end of 2026 remains unlikely. A sudden health crisis, unanticipated leadership fracture, or major external shock could still shift dynamics, though no such verified developments have materialized in the past year.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Democratic presidential nomination for 2028 remains wide open nearly two years after the prior contest, with no major candidates having declared and market prices clustered tightly among Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Gavin Newsom, and Jon Ossoff. A recent New Hampshire poll showing Ocasio-Cortez ahead has lifted her implied probability by highlighting progressive base support, while Newsom benefits from high name recognition and fundraising networks as California governor, and Ossoff draws backing as a Senate alternative with appeal in competitive states. DNC calendar adjustments prioritizing South Carolina have redirected early focus toward coalition building and regional strengths without yet triggering endorsements or formal campaigns. This fragmentation across ideological lanes sustains the bunched trader consensus, though upcoming polling shifts, major fundraising reports, or Senate results could quickly create separation among the leaders.
